items.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: But he also works with Marty Grosz and the Orphan Newsboys

ctx.x: It’s almost like you’re not hearing the chord as much as you are the — almost the washboard effect.

It depends on who’s playing it. Some players mute the strings, some let them ring. With Marty Grosz you hear the ring of the strings, which is nice. Like that’s the way Eddie Condon played. And with Rebecca Kilgore, she lets the strings ring. And it’s just a nice blend, especially with an acoustic bass. If there’s not lots of micing, that guitar, you can key everything on the rhythm guitar. You sure don’t want to be fighting that if it’s © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
playing all four beats. Easier for me to back off a little bit than for the guitar, so you don’t have that. And those two are two of the easiest to work with I can think of.
